A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LancBiO and contain readable main text and Appendices A–I. Algorithms, experiments, equations, and figures can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic optimization, MNIST data hyper-cleaning, and 20Newsgroups hyperparameter-selection experiments, including sensitivity and mini-batch studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds dataset comparisons, dimension-scaling results, and a nonconvex synthetic experiment.

M1.justification: SubBiO, LancBiO, and the dynamic Lanczos subroutine retain their update rules. The least-squares MINRES adaptation tested as LancBiO-MINRES in v2 was already specified in v1 Appendix D. Revised theoretical step-size conditions do not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds Fashion-MNIST clothing images and Kuzushiji-MNIST Japanese characters to hyper-cleaning evaluation, alongside retained MNIST and 20Newsgroups experiments. Appendix I.3 also evaluates a new synthetic problem with a nonconvex lower level, substantially extending the tested problem coverage.

E2.justification: F2SA and HJFBiO join the retained MNIST and 20Newsgroups accuracy/loss comparisons, adding first-order and Hessian/Jacobian-free alternatives. Their participation is visible in v2 Table 1 and Figures 4 and 6. Existing comparators remain; the residual-norm comparisons do not add these two methods.

E3.justification: Existing splits, batching procedures, tuning ranges, and Table 1 measurement times are retained. Added protocols include synthetic dimensions 10, 100, 1000, and 10000 with final objective/runtime reporting, plus a dimension-100 nonconvex experiment using a necessary-condition-based optimality metric.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained subspace-dimension sensitivity and mini-batch studies, v2 adds a scalability analysis across problem dimensions in Table 2 and a nonconvex MINRES case study in Figure 13. These examine computational scaling and behavior outside the strongly convex lower-level setting.

E5.justification: Both versions state averaging over 10 runs, report means and standard deviations in Table 1, and use seed 4 for the subspace sensitivity illustration. The added results do not introduce a different run-count policy, significance test, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All seven original Table 1 rows retain their numerical values. New rows report F2SA and HJFBiO accuracies of 88.65% and 89.30% at corruption rate 0.8, respectively. Additional results include their 20Newsgroups curves, two new image datasets, the scaling table, and the nonconvex optimality curve.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Assumptions 3.10 and 3.11 concerning epoch perturbations and bounded lower-level gradients. Theorem 3.13 becomes Theorem 3.11, retaining O(epsilon^-1) complexity while changing theta from O(m^-4) to O(m^-1) and revising warm-up conditions. Appendices G–H substantially revise the bounds and introduce a Lyapunov-based convergence proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 retain the core contributions: introducing subspace techniques into bilevel optimization, dynamically approximating inverse-Hessian products, averaging 1+1/m Hessian-vector products per iteration, and obtaining O(epsilon^-1) convergence. Added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets added experiments as evidence of robustness across datasets and dimensions and potential applicability to nonconvex problems. Appendix I.1 newly clarifies that initialization Assumption 3.9 is not enforced experimentally. The separate conclusion disappears, but the deterministic focus and stochastic qualifications remain elsewhere.

D1.justification: v2 specifies a finite-difference step of 10^-5 for HJFBiO and discloses that the theoretical initialization requirement is not used in practice. Hardware, code-access information, subspace-dimension schedules, and existing experimental tuning instructions are retained.

R1.justification: New references cover added datasets and comparators, additional applications, and a short distributed-bilevel discussion in Appendix A citing Kong, He, and Zhu. The central positioning relative to Krylov methods and implicit differentiation remains. Several other bibliographic changes update existing works' publication details.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording, reorders the hyper-cleaning and synthetic discussions, adds an Appendix H proof roadmap and acknowledgments, and removes the separate conclusion. Author order and conference front matter change. Most introductory and algorithmic exposition retains its structure and wording.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column conference layout. v1 Figures 1–2 merge into v2 Figure 1, and the 20Newsgroups plot moves from the appendix into the main text. New experimental figures and Table 2 are added, while Table 1 and comparison legends expand.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, datasets, and analyses improve empirical support. However, v1 explicitly assumes epoch perturbation control in Assumption 3.10; v2 removes it, while Appendix H's derivation of Equation (64) uses an error index after warm-up even though Section 3.1 defines the perturbation maximum over all steps starting at 1. The exclusion of earlier errors is not justified. This unresolved step in the strengthened convergence argument prevents a reliable net assessment against the empirical gains.
